title: Office visits: gut, skin, feet and teeth

source.citation: Written for Blackout, 2026-10-09, from the ABFM 2025 In-Training Examination critiques, items 1, 3, 6, 13 and 16. Each question cites its item. Provisional grouping; review before trusting.

questions.q: Which drug has the best evidence for the typical symptoms of diarrhoea-predominant IBS?
questions.why: It covers diarrhoea, pain and bloating, with few adverse effects and a high price. Amitriptyline and dicyclomine often help but with weaker evidence.

questions.q: How long is a course of rifaximin for diarrhoea-predominant IBS?
questions.why: Repeated for recurrence. Linaclotide and lubiprostone are constipation-predominant drugs, and the diarrhoea linaclotide causes is why many patients stop it.

questions.q: Vesicles and bullae on the hands, face and genitals two days after camping. What is prescribed?
questions.why: Face, genitals or bullae mean systemic treatment. Potent topicals do nothing for bullae and are contraindicated on the face and genitals; triamcinolone, if used, goes intramuscularly, since subcutaneous injection causes lipoatrophy.

questions.q: What commonly follows a 5-day methylprednisolone pack for extensive poison ivy?
questions.why: A type IV reaction needs enough dose for long enough, and rebound is the sign the course was too short, not that the diagnosis was wrong.

questions.q: Why does a poison ivy rash seem to spread over several days?
questions.a: Different areas got different amounts of resin and react at different times
d: It passes from person to person
questions.why: Onset is 12 to 72 hours after contact and needs prior sensitisation. Blister fluid contains no urushiol, so draining bullae has no place.

questions.q: A fifth metatarsal shaft fracture in a healthy adult who can bear weight. What is the treatment?
questions.a: Weight-bearing in a boot for 3 to 6 weeks
d: Non-weight-bearing in a boot for 3 to 6 weeks
A short leg cast for 6 weeks
questions.why: A hard-soled shoe serves as well as the boot. Orthopaedics is for a fracture that needs reduction, or for nonunion at six months.

questions.q: Which foot fractures are managed in a short leg cast rather than a boot?
questions.a: Proximal fifth metatarsal and tarsal fractures
questions.why: Foot fractures are about a third of adult lower-limb fractures. Nonunion, malunion, arthritis and compartment syndrome are the complications to warn about.

questions.q: A teething 6-month-old in a town without fluoridated water. Besides a fluoride supplement, what is advised?
questions.a: Brushing with a rice-sized smear of fluoride toothpaste
d: Varnish once a year from age 1
Varnish twice a year from age 3
questions.why: Pea-sized from age 3. Mouthwash waits until 6, when a child can reliably spit, since swallowed fluoride causes fluorosis.

questions.q: How often is fluoride varnish applied to a child at usual caries risk?
questions.why: Every 3 months at high risk, starting with the first tooth in both cases.

questions.q: Cervical screening rates lag the other cancer screens. What is the first step of the improvement project?
questions.a: Find out what the barriers are
d: Set up chart review and outreach to overdue patients
questions.why: Patient-specific reminders at the point of care are the intervention most likely to work later, but a fix chosen before the cause is known tends to miss it.
